chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ali ibn Ribat and Al-Husayn ibn Hashim and Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ays ibn Al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the orphan girl, when should her wealth be handed over to her? He said: When you know that she will neither spoil it nor waste it.
So I asked him, if she had married? He said: If she were to get married, the possession (authority) of the executor is cut-off from her.
ai.seo_question: When should an orphan girl's wealth be handed over to her according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that the release of an orphan's wealth hinges on practical financial prudence ('not spoiling or wasting') rather than mere biological maturity, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of 'bulugh' (adulthood) being tied to 'rushd' (sound judgment). Furthermore, the immediate cessation of the guardian's authority upon marriage highlights the legal transition of financial independence, a nuance distinct from some other schools of thought that may link guardianship solely to age or specific milestones.
